title: Smallest String With A Given Numeric Value
summary: The numeric value of a lowercase character is its position in the alphabet (1-indexed).
statement: The numeric value of a lowercase character is its position in the alphabet (1-indexed). The numeric value of a string is the sum of its characters' values. Given integers n and k, find the lexicographically smallest string of length n with a numeric value of k. A string x is lexicographically smaller than y if x precedes y in dictionary order, either as a prefix or by the first differing character's order.
constraints: Character values are a=1 through z=26; return the lexicographically smallest length-n string totaling k.
hints: Start from the minimum string of all a characters, then place required extra value as far right as possible.
Fill suffix positions with up to 25 extra value each.
Set remaining=k-n; scan right to left, adding min(25,remaining) at each position.
Moving any increment from an earlier position to a later available position strictly decreases the string lexicographically.
editorial: Moving any increment from an earlier position to a later available position strictly decreases the string lexicographically.

tests.explanation: Keep the earliest positions at a and put the remaining value into the suffix, producing aay.
Filling from the right produces aaszz, the smallest valid string.
